claim: The J-lens surfaces unspoken intermediate steps better than the logit lens
published: J-lens beats logit / tuned lens; intermediates (21, 42) become readable in middle layers (Claude)
ours: best rank of the intermediate token at the last position: median 4 (J-lens) vs 9 (logit lens); top-10 for 3/3 vs 2/3
criterion: J-lens median rank lower than the logit lens's and ≥ half of intermediates reach the top 10
post_hoc: arithmetic case removed from the metric after its ranks had been seen

claim: Swapping J-lens coordinates swaps the concept
published: France → China swaps change capital/language/continent answers together (76/192 top-1 across functions, Claude)
ours: layer 11: target answer in top-5 for 12% of 8 prompts (random direction 0%)
criterion: ≥ 50% and ≥ 30 points above the random-direction swap

claim: Swapping J-space coefficients (paper-style sparse NNLS decomposition) swaps the concept
published: category ("think of a {category}") swap with the J-space component: 59% top-5 vs 5% for the non-J component (Claude)
ours: layer 9: target answer in top-5 for 12% of 8 prompts (random vector 0%)
criterion: ≥ 50% and ≥ 30 points above the random-vector swap (amendment 2026-11-27, same thresholds)
post_hoc: paper-style swap added after the pre-stated swap failed

claim: Confirmatory: on 24 fresh two-hop prompts the J-lens ranks the unspoken intermediate better than the logit lens
published: J-lens beats the logit lens at surfacing unspoken intermediates (Claude)
ours: J-lens better on 16, logit lens better on 6, tied on 2 of 24 prompts (sign test p = 0.0525); median best rank 5 vs 8; top-10 for 15 vs 14
criterion: J-lens better on more prompts than the reverse and two-sided sign test p < 0.05 (pre-stated 2026-11-28 before running)
